operations.comment: ; CPU aliases below retain encoded addresses; effective bank context follows each frozen map view.
; RAM aliases describe mechanical roles and can share storage between scenes.
; iNES header: mapper1,128KiB PRG and128KiB CHR, no trainer. Header bytes remain exact.
; SoundTickVector
; Entry trampoline into the per-frame sound sequencer.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundRequestVector
; Entry trampoline for sound selection with temporary request mode.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundMultiply8
; Multiply the byte in sound scratch C1 by C4 using eight shift/add steps; the high and low result occupy C1:C2.
; Scratch is shared with sound pointers.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundInlineDispatch
; A selects a little-endian target from words immediately after the caller return address. Pops that return
; address and tail-jumps through C1:C2; payload bytes are not an ordinary continuation.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundTick
; Skip work when sound control bit0 is set. Otherwise advance stream timing, visit four channels, then
; accumulate the signed fade control. Preserve the channel-enable mask across its shifting iteration.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSilenceChannel
; Map reversed low two channel-index bits to APU register groups; write the silent volume value, with triangle
; using zero.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundWriteRegister
; Translate channel X and register offset Y to an APU address; preserve A while calculating the register index.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundRequest
; Temporarily set sound control bit0 while decoding a request, then restore it.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSelectSequence
; Commands F0 and above use an inline dispatch. Other requests wrap against the sequence count, read a pointer
; and compare its priority before replacing stream state. A zero first byte selects the initialization path.
; Exact tune identities remain unresolved.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundInitializePointers
; Finish clearing channel arrays, then read four effect-stream pointers as high/low byte pairs. These share the
; stream reader scratch; no extra header is skipped.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundInitialize
; Reset tempo/fade and channel work arrays for a zero initialization header, then load four effect pointers from
; high/low byte pairs. Continue through the shared channel-enable initialization.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundControlDispatch
; Preserve Y and dispatch the low three command bits through an inline target list.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; Eight little-endian handler addresses for the low three global command bits. Inline dispatch removes its
; return address; these words are payload, not fallthrough instructions.
; SoundStopSequence
; Clear stream, priority and auxiliary state; invert selected channel bits before silencing the disabled
; channels.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundClearEffectPointers
; Clear both halves of all four effect pointers; the enable-mask path subsequently marks only active effect
; channels dirty.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundApplyEnableMask
; Visit four reversed APU channels and silence those absent from the mask; then initialize sweep and enable all
; four tone/noise channels.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundPauseResume
; Set or clear sound-control bit1. The pause path also clears active duration; the mask command normalizes a
; shifted channel mask and preserves the all-channel sentinel.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSetPitchScale
; Negate the command parameter into the global pitch-scale byte.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundReadSequenceEvent
; Decrement active duration, or consume an event mask from the sequence stream. Optional fields update stream
; looping, transpose and note timing; multiplication derives a gate duration. Channel-mask changes refresh
; silencing before the new mask is committed.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundUpdateChannel
; Resolve the channel instrument, update its envelope, and stop notes when duration expires. In command mode
; consume a bitmask of per-channel changes and then a note/rest byte.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundChannelCommandDispatch
; Dispatch a channel command through five little-endian inline field-setter targets. Supported field masks
; select these five entries; arbitrary higher mask bits have no established contract.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; Five little-endian field-setter targets for packed channel commands. Only the supported five command bits have
; valid entries; higher mask bits are not validated.
; SoundDecodeNote
; A zero note clears envelope timing. Other notes mark pitch dirty, choose a portamento parameter and either
; calculate a tone period or select a noise value. Music and effects share these channel arrays.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundReadStreamByte
; Read through D0:D1 and advance the 16-bit sequence pointer, carrying into its high byte.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundUpdateEffectStream
; Select the effect half of the channel arrays, subtract tempo from note/gate timers and parse more commands
; when they expire. Packed notes combine a duration class with a five-bit note; zero is a rest.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEffectCommandDispatch
; Commands below four have no extra byte; later commands fetch a parameter before inline dispatch through
; twenty-five handler targets. Commands beyond the supported table remain invalid/uncertain.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; Twenty-five little-endian effect command targets. The decoder permits a wider five-bit value, but values25..31
; have no established entry contract.
; SoundToggleEffectFlags
; Toggle duration/style bits or set the triplet-like duration flag in the effect channel control byte. The exact
; authored command names are unknown.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEffectSetLoopTarget
; Clear loop state and read a two-byte effect address into the saved loop target. Other nearby handlers replace
; duration, style and transpose parameters.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEffectCountedBranch
; Four entry points select one of four per-channel counters. An exhausted counter either reloads the command
; count or falls through; a taken loop reads a target pointer, while the untaken path skips its two bytes. The
; command class distinguishes finite repeats from the alternate terminating form.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEffectMergeFlags
; Replace selected effect control bits with the command parameter. The terminating entry discards the dispatch
; return, clears this stream pointer and returns through the channel-silencing path.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundReadEffectByte
; Form a pointer from the split per-channel stream arrays and increment that pointer after reading one byte.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; Seven short-duration values selected by packed note classes1..7 after subtracting one. Alternate timing mode
; uses this table instead of the ordinary duration table.
; Seven ordinary packed-note duration values; class zero is handled separately by the interpreter.
; Eight signed relative-note adjustments selected by the low three command bits.
; SoundReleaseEnvelope
; Replace low envelope-state bits with release state3, preserving the channel flags.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundRestartEnvelope
; Clear the envelope state; triangle channels get special timing from the current duration and channel volume
; multiplier. Preserve the note index in Y.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundNoteToPeriod
; Clamp the note index below 60h, track pitch changes and load a 16-bit period from the note table. Special
; cases preserve or reset portamento/envelope state.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundResetModulation
; Clear modulation phase only when the instrument or channel flags request it; retain the other channel control
; bits.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSetVolume
; Merge the parameter with duty/volume control except for the triangle-specific path.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSetInstrument
; Store the instrument number, mark its parameters dirty, and compute its eight-byte record pointer from the
; shared bank-local instrument base.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSetFinePitch
; Store the signed fine-pitch adjustment for the indexed channel.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundSetDuty
; Keep the low volume nibble and combine duty/control bits with constant volume mode.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEnvelopeDispatch
; Dispatch the low three envelope-state bits while retaining the current amplitude in scratch C4.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; Five envelope state targets: initialize, attack, decay, sustain/release handling and completion. Corrupt
; states beyond the monotone supported state sequence are not validated.
; SoundEnvelopeAttack
; Add a table-selected rate until amplitude saturates at F0h, then advance envelope state.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEnvelopeDecay
; Subtract the instrument decay rate, clamping at its sustain threshold and advancing state when reached.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundEnvelopeRelease
; Subtract the release rate until zero; triangle follows a separate direct zero path. Every finished stage
; advances the low state bits.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundRenderEnvelope
; Combine envelope amplitude, fade, duty and channel volume; write the APU volume/control register. Effects and
; music select different fade handling.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundRenderPitch
; Apply instrument modulation to the base period, optionally add the global pitch scale, convert to APU timer
; bits and suppress unchanged high-register writes to avoid retriggering length counters.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; SoundAdvancePortamento
; If pitch-dirty is set, move the base period using a signed step. Clear that flag at completion, then advance
; the instrument modulation phase with carry toggling direction bits.
; Entry physical PRG bank 0; supplied physical slot banks [0, 1, 14, 15]. Bank writes can change subsequent CPU
; aliases.
; Thirty-two envelope step values. Instrument attack/decay/release fields index this curve; these are amplitude
; rates rather than CPU targets.
; Eight quantized pitch thresholds used by the portamento calculation. The final two overlap the nominal period
; base but are outside the nonzero note-period access domain.
; Quantized sixteen-bit tone periods accessed through overlapping low/high bases. Nonzero notes are clamped
; below60h and incremented before doubling; the declared physical interval preserves the reviewed exact
; boundary. No original tuning-system formula is asserted.
; Uniform zero bytes bounded by reviewed adjacent structures. No consumer or authored fill purpose is
; established.
; Positive sequence count64, used to wrap ordinary sound requests before indexing the pointer list.
; Big-endian CPU base pointer to eight-byte instrument records; this byte order differs from ordinary
; little-endian 6502 pointers.
; Sixty-four high/low CPU pointer pairs for music/effect initialization headers. Request wrapping bounds the
; index; sequence identity and natural selection of every request remain unknown.
; Forty-seven eight-byte instrument records. Consumers use envelope rate/sustain fields, volume/duty, modulation
; and control flags. Record indexing multiplies by eight; bytes are shared by music and effects. Original
; instrument names are unknown.
; Sound initialization headers and interpreter bytecode, with event masks, packed note/duration values and
; effect command operands. Initialization headers hold four big-endian channel pointers; effect substreams use
; their own command/stop grammar. Structurally parsed streams do not prove natural playback of every tune. Small
; disconnected stop/tail records retain generic data meaning.
; Uniform zero bytes bounded by reviewed adjacent structures. No consumer or authored fill purpose is

; Low bytes of104 palette-stream CPU pointers, paired by index with the high-byte plane. Palette selectors
; require the supported index domain.
; Eight zero bytes between independently bounded pointer planes. No authored fill purpose is known.
; High bytes of104 palette-stream CPU pointers. The pointed records begin with a RAM palette destination and end
; at a negative byte.
; Palette records: initial destination index followed by nonnegative NES palette bytes and a negative
; terminator. The loader may mask four-color groups before marking upload pending; palette names remain unknown.

; Replicated reset wrapper: disable interrupts, perform the mapper reset write through an INC at FFD9, and jump
